questions.q: What is the standard magnification of the gemmologist's loupe?
questions.why: It is the standard magnification to judge a stone.

questions.q: Why wipe the stone with the chamois before looking at it?
choices: Dust and grease leave a film that would be mistaken for a flaw
questions.why: A wrong reading on a dirty stone is beginners' mistake number 1.

questions.q: Why turn the stone in all directions?
choices: An inclusion or a fracture cannot be seen from every angle
questions.why: You look through the table, the sides and from below.

questions.q: What do you NOT note with the loupe?
questions.why: The index is measured with the refractometer.

questions.q: What characterizes a dirty stone under the loupe?
choices: A whitish film on the surface

questions.q: What should you do with a stone that looks veiled?
choices: Note the film as a flaw
Wipe it, then look at it again
questions.why: Note nothing before cleaning the stone.

questions.q: The luster of a stone is…
choices: the way its surface returns light
